messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT alert — Elevated 5xx and connection timeouts observed for inference-hosting in eu-central-1 (single AZ). Auto-remediation attempted (drain+replace) failed due to ENI attach errors. Notify on-call immediately.
Emma H.: on it. paging Raj and Leo. seeing a spike in latency for model 'redwood-13b' routes.
Raj Patel: ack. I'm connected. what's the primary symptom? 5xx from runtime or network TCP resets?
Maria G.: customers reporting inference timeouts and stalled streams. Dashboard: request success rate down ~35% over last 12m.
Jordan L.: I see repeated ERR_CONNECTION_RESET in the runtime logs. Kernel-level ENI detach/attach errors in EC2 events stream.
Leo K.: AWS health: no broad region outage, but there are EC2 instance status checks failing in eu-central-1a. Looks like a single AZ partial network degradation.
oncall-uk: taking ownership as primary on-call for infra. Emma, Raj — can you start mitigation steps?
Emma H.: started scaling up warm nodes in eu-central-1b (cross-AZ) but routing is still sending a lot of traffic to eu-central-1a. Need to adjust traffic routing at the load balancer/route53 level.
Raj Patel: pushing route change plan: 1) shift ~60% traffic to eu-central-1b via NLB target weights, 2) enable Route53 failover policy to prefer healthy endpoints, 3) expand connection timeout retry backoff. Any objections?
Leo K.: NLB target weight changes OK. but note: some customer-dedicated pools pinned to AZ; we need to check Dedicated customers in that AZ.
Maria G.: CustomerImpact matrix: 8 Dedicated tenants pinned in eu-central-1a (SLOs impacted), and many hosted API calls from EU are hitting that AZ. We should flag high-priority customers.
Jordan L.: rolling a canary of a more defensive connection retry in the runtime is cheap — I'll push a config toggle to bypass the broken ENIs: ``/api/v1/configs/reconnect_backoff=1.5``
Emma H.: executing NLB weight change now: ``aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:btg --attributes Key=weight,Value=40`` (this is a simulated cmd for the thread)
incident-bot: Deploy workflow triggered: traffic-shift -> health-check monitor.
Raj Patel: Route53 failover: creating a secondary record pointing to eu-central-1b set with health check TTL=30s. running: ``aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://failover.json``
Leo K.: NOTE: customer pinned pools require manual migration. I'll open a migration job and message the SEs.
Maria G.: on customer comms: drafting a message for the affected tenants. severity: degraded service, not fully down. ETA for mitigation?
Emma H.: after weight change, error rate reduced from 35% to ~14% in 8 minutes. streaming still unstable for long-lived connections.
Jordan L.: investigating NLB connection reuse and TCP keepalive. There's a pattern of mid-connection resets whenever ENI flips.
Raj Patel: I've requested AWS support escalation for the failed ENI attach/tainting. Ticket opened — case #20378492. aws-support-bot: Hello — we see your case and assigned an engineer. Please provide instance IDs and logs.
Leo K.: provided instance IDs + ENI attach failure logs. Also asked for any visible hypervisor-level network flaps.
Maria G.: Customer notify drafted: "We’re seeing higher-than-normal inference timeouts in eu-central-1 due to zonal network instability. We’re shifting traffic to healthy AZs and working with AWS." Sharing in #customer-notify for review.
oncall-uk: Handoff incoming in ~30m to US oncall. Emma/Leo please summarize actions for them.
Emma H.: Summary: 1) Traffic shifted to eu-central-1b via NLB weight change + Route53 failover. 2) Canaries for connection retry enabled. 3) Dedicated tenant migrations in progress (manual). 4) AWS support engaged for ENI attach errors.
Raj Patel: Mitigation metrics: success rate up to 88% post-shift; average tail latency improved ~200ms. But for customers pinned to the affected AZ we'll need either manual migration or emergency Dedicated fallback (read-only?).
Jordan L.: pushed temporary runtime patch to reduce active connection reuse; this reduces streaming resets but increases CPU. Monitor CPU in eu-central-1b.
incident-bot: Monitoring alert — cpu usage for runtime pool in eu-central-1b at 78% (warning).
Leo K.: autoscaling policy updated to accelerate warm pool spin-up for eu-central-1b. Config snippet: ``"warm_pool_desired": 6 -> 12"``
Maria G.: Uploaded customer impact list to shared doc and tagged CS. tagging: @cs-team please review priority list and start outreach for top 3 tenants.
Emma H.: AWS has confirmed an internal networking disruption in eu-central-1a causing ENI attach delays; they're recommending instance replacement or migration out of the AZ.
Raj Patel: Next steps: continue shifting traffic + migrate Dedicated tenants off AZ. If AWS can't restore, plan for scheduled maintenance migration overnight.
oncall-uk: handing to US on-call (Leo K.) in 25m. Please keep the incident channel updated and flag any regression.
Leo K.: taking over. Will coordinate final migrations and confirm when all pinned tenants are moved.
Maria G.: CS updated major tenants and provided temporary credits for affected windows.
Emma H.: marking the incident as mitigated for hosted API traffic. Persisting work for Dedicated tenant migrations. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: INCIDENT update — status: mitigated (partial). Primary cause: zonal network instability (eu-central-1a). Actions: traffic shifted, AWS engaged, Dedicated migrations ongoing.
Raj Patel: leaving detailed log snippets here for postmortem.
Jordan L.: dropping a few log excerpts: ``[runtime] stream-reset: code=ECONNRESET src=eni-attach-failed``
Leo K.: I'll open a follow-up thread for full postmortem and RCA once AWS gives final root cause.
Maria G.: thanks everyone — great coordination. I'll schedule a customer-facing summary after the RCA. :bow:
